chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: The Lion's compliment about knowing when to lay out
summary: Willie the Lion told Danny he was the one guitarist who knew when to lay out, and describes how the Lion's key shifts could trick accompanists.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: See, the Lion said Jelly Roll couldn't play no piano, you know. Like, the Lion is fantastic. The Lion's playing eight-beat, trick you. The Lion paid me a compliment I'll never forget. He said, "Do you why know I like you, Danny? I like your playing." I said, "Why?" I said, "What about it? I can't play." He said, "No. You just know how to lay out." He said, "You're one of the first...you're about the only guitar player I know who knows when to lay out." You know, like you get to playin' something that's tricky; you know, somebody might ..(?)..
"Well, you're cool. You don't be runnin' through there. I'd know I can(?) lift my hand." And they'd respect you for that.

I used to work at the Central Plaza. He said, "You're the only one. The rest of them, they're in there, and they ain't watching what they're doing." But you got to respect the Lion, 'cause the Lion is movin'.
He's in A and he's in E, you know, and they want to get you out, see. He'd play, and he'd hit a definite [HUMS EXTENDED NOTE], and you'd play in that key -- and it's somewhere else.
Yeah. You're lucky if you understand it. But Jelly had a thing, you know.
He'd go like this. [DEMONSTRATES] And he's gone, in another key.
